evidence.quoted_text:
def atomic(filename, data):
    filename = Path(filename)
    durable_directory(filename.parent)
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(dir=filename.parent, delete=False) as stream:
        stream.write(data)
        stream.flush()
        os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        temporary = stream.name
    os.replace(temporary, filename)
    fsync_dir(filename.parent)
evidence.reason: The current `atomic` implementation creates a temp file with `delete=False`, then performs write/flush/fsync and `os.replace` without any `try`/`finally` cleanup. If any of those operations raises, the named staging file remains on disk, and a retry creates another one. This is an ordinary correctness/resource-leak defect in existing intended atomic-write behavior, not a new requirement. The fix can be local: capture the temp path and unlink it on failure, while keeping the post-replace directory sync.
